researcher_notes: Method: official texts were opened on datafiles.chinhphu.vn / vanban.chinhphu.vn / an official provincial portal (hcc.nghean.gov.vn) and moit.gov.vn; scanned signed PDFs were rendered page by page and read directly (no OCR guesswork). The shared web-search budget ran out part-way through, so the E-commerce Law, the Competition Law text, a possible new 2026 labelling decree and VN enforcement cases could not be checked; those are marked SECONDARY/UNVERIFIED or listed in gaps. CORRECTIONS to existing team docs: (1) NĐ 24/2025/NĐ-CP took effect on signing, 21/02/2025 (Điều 4.1 of the signed text); the 10/04/2025 date cited in sources/2026-10-05 A.3.1 is wrong. (2) The misleading-consumer-information fine is NĐ 98/2020 Điều 47 khoản 2 điểm a as rewritten by NĐ 24/2025: 20–30 million VND (the knowledge doc listed it as UNVERIFIED). (3) The Advertising Law's implementing decree is NĐ 342/2025/NĐ-CP (signed 26/12/2025, effective 15/02/2026, repeals NĐ 181/2013 and NĐ 70/2021); the advertising sanctions decree is now NĐ 87/2026/NĐ-CP (effective 15/05/2026). The knowledge doc still points at NĐ 38/2021. (4) Competition sanctions NĐ 75/2019 were amended by NĐ 102/2026/NĐ-CP (effective 20/05/2026). KEY DESIGN POINT for Thảo: amended Luật Quảng cáo Điều 19 khoản 3 điểm b (Law 75/2025) says advertising content does NOT include content that must be publicly disclosed or provided under other laws. Read literally, the mandatory parts of an annual report (TT 96/2020 Phụ lục IV) fall outside 'advertising', while the same claims reused in marketing fall inside. This supports the team's rule of treating consumer/advertising law as context, not as a basis for a violation finding. No VN rule defines 'greenwashing' or sets specific environmental-claim criteria. The only certification route for a 'thân thiện môi trường' product claim found in this area is the Vietnam Ecolabel (NĐ 08/2022 Điều 145–150, procedure amended by NĐ 48/2026).
gaps: E-commerce Law 2025 (lead: 122/2025/QH15, effective 2026-07-01): number, dates and provisions not verified; web-search budget ran out before an official page was found.

Whether a new goods-labelling decree replacing NĐ 43/2017 (as amended by NĐ 111/2021) was issued in 2025–2026 to implement electronic labels / digital product passports under Law 78/2025 Điều 34a: not checked.
Implementing decrees of Law 78/2025 (quality) and Law 70/2025 (standards): QĐ 2138/QĐ-TTg planned issue before 2025-12-01; whether and when they were issued is not verified.
NĐ 87/2026/NĐ-CP: signed text not opened. The exact title, the article and fine for misleading advertising content, and whether it repeals NĐ 38/2021 (as amended by NĐ 129/2021) are unconfirmed.
NĐ 98/2020/NĐ-CP: effective date and the general rule on individual vs organisation fine levels were not re-read.
Luật Cạnh tranh 23/2018/QH14: official text not opened; Điều 45 numbering and the adoption/effective dates are SECONDARY or background only.
NĐ 55/2024/NĐ-CP: article-level content not read (scanned 38-page PDF); only metadata verified.
No Vietnamese enforcement decision with published verbatim wording of a misleading environmental/green claim was found (search budget exhausted; the 2026-10-05 session also found none).
Bộ luật Hình sự Điều 197 (quảng cáo gian dối): not checked.
Public URLs for (a) the National Competition Commission's list of businesses that violated consumer rights and (b) MAE's list of Vietnam Ecolabel-certified products were not located.
Whether MOIT's draft law amending the Commercial, Foreign Trade, Competition and Consumer Protection laws was sent to the National Assembly after July 2026: unknown.
TCVN adoption of ISO 14021 (self-declared environmental claims): number/year not verified; it is a voluntary standard but the most specific technical reference for claims such as 'có thể tái chế'.

MOIT is drafting an amending law (see VN-DUTHAO-LUAT-SUADOI-TM-QLNT-CT-BVQLNTD-2026); the proposals published so far concern personal data, standard-form contracts and local-government roles, not misleading information.

key_provisions.summary: Defines người có ảnh hưởng (influencer): experts, reputable or socially followed persons.
Defines tiêu dùng bền vững (sustainable consumption) as use of goods/services that meets needs while minimising negative environmental and socio-economic impacts.

Prohibits deceiving or misleading consumers through false, incomplete or inaccurate information about the product, the business's reputation or capacity, transaction terms, or images, papers and certification documents of competent state agencies.

Businesses must give accurate, complete information on measurement, quantity, quality, uses, price and origin, and must label goods truthfully, clearly and accurately, reflecting the true nature of the goods.

A third party that carries product information must ensure accuracy, ask the business for documents proving accuracy, and is jointly liable for inaccurate information unless it took all legally required verification steps.
Influencers must meet the third-party duties and tell consumers in advance that they are sponsored.
Effective 01/07/2024.

key_provisions.summary: Redefines advertising; defines người chuyển tải sản phẩm quảng cáo as a person who directly advertises, recommends or endorses products online or by wearing, attaching or displaying them for profit.
Prohibits comparing one's products with the same type of products of others without lawful substantiating documents.

Ad conveyors must follow consumer-protection and product-information rules, hand over related documents on request, and are legally responsible if content breaches Điều 19. Influencers must also verify the advertiser's reliability, check product documents, not promote products they have not used or do not understand, and announce the advertising before and during it.

Advertising content must be truthful, accurate and clear and must not mislead about features, quality, uses or effects; required notes and warnings must be as legible and audible as the rest of the ad.
Advertising content excludes mandatory label content, content that must be publicly disclosed or provided to customers, and content belonging to information-provision duties under other laws.
Commercial advertising is now governed by advertising law; repeals Section 2, Chapter IV of the Commercial Law.
Effective 01/01/2026; pending billboard/banner notifications follow the old law.

Mandatory content per special product (e.g. pesticides: active ingredient, uses, hazard warnings; feed, aquaculture-environment and livestock-waste products: name, features, responsible entity; household chemicals: registration holder, warnings); cosmetics ads must match the declared product features.
Non-fixed online ads must close with one interaction; no fake or hard-to-distinguish close buttons; no wait to close static image ads and at most 5 seconds for animated/video ads.

Online ad service providers (domestic and cross-border) notify MOCST before operating; keep ad records, including documents related to the advertised product, for 3 years; report annually to MOCST by 25 November; search/intermediary platforms must label sponsored results.
Licences under the old decrees stay valid; decree effective 15/02/2026; repeals NĐ 181/2013 and NĐ 70/2021.

amends: Luật Chất lượng sản phẩm, hàng hóa 05/2007/QH12

key_provisions.summary: Defines hộ chiếu số của sản phẩm (digital product passport): product and supply-chain information stored in a barcode or linked database, readable by suitable devices.
Goods are classified by risk into low, medium and high risk.
Traceability and supply-chain transparency must be truthful, objective, authentic and verifiable; mandatory for high-risk goods on a roadmap set by each ministry; encouraged for others.
Technology in quality management: barcodes, traceability, electronic labels, digital passports and AI/big data, in line with the digital and circular economy; data must be secure.

Prohibits false information or advertising and deception about quality, origin and provenance (especially on digital platforms); concealing risk information affecting health, property or the environment; quality-related unfair competition causing confusion.
Producers must give truthful quality information, declare applicable standards, and label goods physically, electronically or by digital passport with traceability information.

Goods in circulation must carry physical/electronic labels or a digital passport with barcode, traceability and quality information and be updated in the electronic data system; online sellers and platform operators have information and complaint-handling duties.

key_provisions.summary: Application dossier (valid 6 months); completeness check within 4 days and assessment within 26 days of a complete dossier by an evaluation council, with site survey or expert testing if needed; written reasons if refused.
